tasks.short: Review costs and revenues after the close and say what the forecast should assume.

today.trigger: The monthly AFAS close locks, or FP&A asks before the forecast lock what a cost line should assume. Typical lines are flex labour, fuel, warehouse overtime and site housing.
steps: Export the profit and loss from AFAS by site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo), cost centre and account.
Add open purchase commitments, the lease schedule and the three agency contracts.
Compare actuals in Excel with last year and with the latest forecast.
Separate one-offs such as a damage claim, a CAO back-pay or a single large spot job.
Send the controller and FP&A a short note on what next period should assume.
drudgery: Rebuilding last month's workbook from a copy.
Re-aligning cost centres that moved since the budget.
Rewriting the same variance sentences for fuel, flex and overtime.
today.time_sinks: Waiting for a site manager to explain a spike, and discovering that flex labour sits in three agency accounts while the forecast holds one line.

lenses.faster: The bridge from actuals to a run-rate, and a first note on what to assume, are ready the morning the close locks. The accountant checks the bridges and the one-off tags.
lenses.autonomous: The AFAS period lock starts the pack. Nobody has to remember to refresh the workbook.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep a weekly view, by site, of flex labour, fuel and warehouse overtime that FP&A can drop into the forecast the sites are asked to trust.
lenses.joy: The copying and the repeated sentences go away. What remains is the call on which spike is structural.
lenses.options: Each pack carries five assumption sets: volume flat, peak season, a CAO wage step, an agency rate change, and a fuel move, each tied to an account.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets the rules for a one-off and the drivers the projection must use (orders, shifts, kilometres), and reviews the cases those rules get wrong.
reach: First-pass driver commentary that FP&A now writes after the close.
Simple flux lines the controller asks the bookkeepers to explain.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which Rotterdam peak is a customer pattern and which is a one-off claim, and whether a site explanation is complete enough for a forecast the business will trust.
tasks.pattern_why: Actuals and a mechanical run-rate can be built from the nightly extract. The sentence that enters the forecast is a judgment, so the accountant or the controller signs the pack before FP&A uses it.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period lock, or a named FP&A request before the forecast lock.
steps: A job reads the nightly AFAS extract by site, cost centre and account, plus open commitments and the lease register.
Rules apply the one-off list and compute run-rate against the latest forecast.
The draft is a one-page projection and five driver scenarios, each figure tied to an account and a period.
The accountant reviews flagged bridges, edits the advice, and sends breaks back to the site or to FP&A.
The signed pack is filed on SharePoint and linked from the forecast file.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant or the controller signs the pack before FP&A loads it. Any variance above the agreed euro amount stays open until a person has tagged it.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and the cost-centre map by site
One-off log
Volume drivers: orders, kilometres, shifts
Lease schedule and agency rate cards
Latest forecast version
CAO wage-step calendar
in_practice.logs_to: The close folder on SharePoint, with the approver, the time, the forecast version and the account list written on the pack.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reports actuals by administration, cost centre and period, and can store a budget next to those actuals.
Power BI supports a scheduled refresh and variance visuals on a finance dataset.
Noordhaven already refreshes a finance Power BI dashboard from a nightly AFAS extract, so the actuals path is in place.

risks: A wrong cost-centre map produces a clean pack that moves the forecast the wrong way.
CAO wage steps and agency rate cards are not in the ledger. A model that only reads actuals misses the commitment.
Site managers stop explaining spikes if the pack looks finished before they have spoken.
research_questions: Do the two accountants spend about 40 hours a year on this, or does FP&A already own the bridge?
Which forecast lines are in the Power BI model today, and which still live in a personal Excel file?
Are orders, kilometres and shifts in a system the nightly extract can join?
How often does the controller reject a one-off tag after the site has explained it?

tasks.short: Look for weak controls, duplicate spend, fraud and breaches of the rules.

today.trigger: The internal-audit plan, an external-auditor request, a tip, or a close surprise such as a duplicate agency invoice or a margin drop at one site.
steps: Pull the general ledger, payables and the payroll journals from AFAS, and the Rabobank movements.
Download hours and invoices from the three staffing-agency portals.
In Excel, look for duplicate invoice numbers, split purchases under the approval limit, changed supplier IBANs and round-amount claims.
Open the SharePoint policy on purchasing, expenses or agency hiring and mark what the item breaks.
Write the euro amount and discuss it with the controller before it is reported.
drudgery: Downloading the same portal files each month.
Matching IBANs and invoice numbers by hand.
Ticking sample boxes for the external auditor.
today.time_sinks: False hits on legitimate multi-drop and multi-site deliveries, and reading the CAO or the purchasing policy to see whether a posting is allowed.

lenses.faster: Duplicate, IBAN-change, split-invoice and unusual-journal tests run on the extract every night. The accountant opens a short list with the invoice and the policy clause attached.
lenses.autonomous: A new supplier IBAN, a repeated invoice number, or a journal posted by the user who also approved the order opens a case on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every agency invoice and every purchase above a low threshold would be tested each week, and hours ordered, hours invoiced and hours paid would be reconciled for all three agencies.
lenses.joy: The ticking and the downloading go away. What remains is the conversation about why a control failed.
lenses.options: Each exception arrives with a likely benign warehouse explanation, a likely breach, and the euro exposure, so the accountant picks the line worth pursuing.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the test catalogue and the materiality thresholds, and retires tests that only produce noise.
reach: Duplicate-invoice and master-data checks the bookkeepers now do by eye.
The transaction tests the external auditor samples, with the formal opinion still theirs.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a pattern is fraud, a sloppy control, or how a night shift in Venlo actually receives goods. Naming a person is a separate decision, with care under the AVG and the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching rules on AFAS, Rabobank and the agency portals can run unattended. Calling an item a control failure, a fraud suspicion or a policy breach is the accountant's conclusion before it is reported.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly refresh of the AFAS extract, a new agency-portal file, or a Rabobank statement import. A tip or an auditor request can start an extra test.
steps: Rules score payables, journals and bank lines for duplicates, IBAN changes, split amounts, user conflicts and weekend postings.
Agency hours and invoices are matched to what was ordered and to the AFAS accrual.
Items that clear the rules are stored with the test id. Items that fail open a case with the document link and the policy clause.
The accountant marks each case as benign, a control gap, or a suspected breach, and writes the euro exposure.
Confirmed items go to the controller. Anything that names an employee waits for that review.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs anything that will be reported as a finding or a fraud suspicion. Cleared matches stay on the log without a signature.
data_needed: Ledger, payables, bank statements and payment batches
Supplier master history, including IBANs
Approval limits and the user who approved
Agency orders, hours and invoices
Purchasing, expense and agency policies
Materiality thresholds set by the controller
in_practice.logs_to: A finding log in the close folder on SharePoint: test id, transaction ids, conclusion, euro amount, approver and time.

evidence.claim: MindBridge analyses full general-ledger populations for unusual entries.
CaseWare IDEA runs duplicate, gap and exception tests on ledger and payable extracts.
A three-way match of order, invoice and payment, plus an IBAN change check, is a standard payable control and can be expressed as rules.

risks: Night deliveries and multi-site drops look like split invoices and will flood the queue if the rules ignore the warehouse pattern.
Agency files hold names and hours. Using them to chase fraud needs an AVG purpose, a retention limit, and works-council information if the check becomes worker monitoring.
A test that scores named employees for misconduct can fall under the EU AI Act employment category. Keep the tests on transactions, and keep the conclusion with a person.
A missed duplicate above the threshold never reaches the accountant, so a silent rule is a real residual risk.
research_questions: How many duplicate, IBAN or agency-invoice points did the external auditor raise in the last two years, and were they already visible in AFAS?
Can the three agency portals deliver hours and invoices on a schedule?
What euro amount does the controller treat as a finding?
Has the works council already been informed of any systematic review of employee-related transactions?

tasks.short: Compare budgeted cost with actual cost and keep the budget maintained.

today.trigger: Each month, after the AFAS close, the controller wants budget versus actual before the management meeting.
steps: Export actuals from AFAS and open the budget FP&A holds in AFAS or in Excel.
Map accounts and cost centres that moved after the budget was set.
Compute the variance by site and by cost type: own staff, flex, housing, fleet.
Paste the table into the management pack or rebuild it in Power BI.
Write one line on every variance the meeting is likely to ask about.
drudgery: Remapping accounts by hand each month.
Copying tables into a slide pack.
Splitting the single flex-labour budget line across three agency accounts.
today.time_sinks: The budget structure and the ledger structure differ, so a large part of the hour is mapping rather than reading the variance.

lenses.faster: The join of budget to actuals, in the ledger's own structure, is refreshed when the period locks. The accountant writes only on the lines outside the threshold.
lenses.autonomous: The period lock refreshes the pack. No one opens last month's file to start the new one.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every cost centre at the three sites would have a budget-versus-actual and a latest-forecast view each month, in the chart of accounts, in time for the meeting.
lenses.joy: The remapping and the formatting go away. What remains is deciding which overrun is timing and which one a site must explain.
lenses.options: The pack shows the original budget, the latest forecast and the actual, so the meeting can see whether the gap is an old budget or a new miss.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the account map and the threshold rules, and checks the map when FP&A revises the budget or a cost centre changes.
reach: The monthly variance table FP&A rebuilds for the management pack.
The first explanation of a cost-centre miss that bookkeepers now prepare ad hoc.

tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a variance is an agency invoice in the wrong period or a real overrun. The report can show the euros. The accountant still makes that call on material lines.
tasks.pattern_why: Budget versus actual is a join of two structured tables with a threshold and an account map. It can be built once in AFAS and Power BI and run without a model. A person explains only the lines outside the threshold.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period lock for the month.
steps: A scheduled job joins the approved budget and the latest forecast to actuals using the maintained account and cost-centre map.
Flex labour is split by agency. Own staff, housing and fleet stay on their own accounts.
Lines inside the euro threshold publish to the Power BI pack with no commentary.
Lines outside the threshold land on a list with site, account, euros and the share of the total miss.
The accountant writes the commentary on that list and files it with the management pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the commentary on variances outside the threshold before the meeting. Figures inside the threshold refresh on the lock.
data_needed: Approved budget version and latest forecast, stored by account and cost centre
Actuals from the locked period
Account and cost-centre map, including the three agency accounts
Thresholds agreed with the controller
Site codes for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history, plus the variance note in the management-pack folder with the map version and the approver.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can hold a budget and report budget against actual by period and cost centre.
Power BI can present that comparison from a scheduled dataset refresh.
Noordhaven already refreshes Power BI from a nightly AFAS extract.

risks: A wrong map produces a number the meeting will trust more than it trusted the old spreadsheet.
If FP&A revises the forecast and the pack still reads the original budget, the meeting debates the wrong gap.
Site managers can learn the threshold and split spend so that nothing is ever discussed.
research_questions: Is the approved budget stored in AFAS, or only in an FP&A workbook?
How many account codes have moved since the current budget was loaded?
What euro variance does the management meeting actually discuss?
Does FP&A want this pack to show the original budget, the latest forecast, or both?

tasks.short: Check payroll liabilities, premium wage bases and wage-tax compliance.

today.trigger: The payroll specialist posts the period journal, a quarterly or year-end premium true-up is due, or the auditor samples the wage liability. A Whk rate letter or a Belastingdienst query starts the same work.
steps: Take the AFAS payroll journal, the loonaangifte summary and headcount by site.
Check which wage components, including CAO allowances such as shift premiums, enter the premium wage base.
Keep agency flex workers in the agency cost and outside Noordhaven's own Awf, Aof and Whk base.
Tie wage tax, the pension funds the two CAOs require, the leave and vakantiegeld provision, and the sick-pay accrual to the balance sheet.
Send breaks to the payroll specialist and sign the liability that enters the close.
drudgery: Adding up wage components by site.
Rebuilding the leave and vakantiegeld workbook.
Searching mail for the latest Whk rate letter.
today.time_sinks: A wage-component map that was not updated after a CAO change, and flex and own staff mixed on the same cost centre.

lenses.faster: The bridge from payroll components to the loonaangifte and to the balance-sheet accruals is calculated when the journal posts. The accountant reviews the breaks.
lenses.autonomous: Posting of the payroll journal starts the tie-out. A break above the set amount opens a case for the accountant and the payroll specialist.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every wage component would be reconciled every period, and the Whk, leave and sick-pay accruals would stay current so the auditor does not rebuild them at year-end.
lenses.joy: Adding up allowances by site goes away. What remains is the grey wage component, and the talk with payroll when the filing and the ledger disagree.
lenses.options: The pack shows the accrual at the current Whk rates and at the rate on a letter that may still be revised, so Finance sees the range before it books one number.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the wage-component map (premium-bearing or not, own staff or flex) and the accrual method, and reviews the map when the CAO or a rate letter changes.
reach: The payroll accrual journal the bookkeepers post from a payroll summary.
The first check that an agency invoice reflects inlenersbeloning, a check that now falls between Finance and HR.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding how to treat a component the CAO and the tax rules describe differently, and signing the liability in the close. A wrong premium base becomes a Belastingdienst assessment.
tasks.pattern_why: The tie-out is a set of rules on AFAS wage components, but the signed liability is a tax and premium position. The accountant approves each period before the amount is booked. Sick-pay detail under the Wet verbetering poortwachter stays with payroll.

in_practice.trigger: The payroll specialist locks the period and posts the payroll journal in AFAS.
steps: The job reads wage-component totals by site and cost centre, the loonaangifte summary, and the balance-sheet accounts.
The wage-component map classifies each component for Awf, Aof, Whk, pension and the leave provision, and excludes agency flex from the own-staff base.
Breaks above the threshold, and any component not on the map, open a case.
The accountant and the payroll specialist clear the cases. The accountant signs the accrual, including leave, vakantiegeld and sick-pay cost, using totals only.
The signed tie-out is filed in the close folder with the map version and the rate letter used.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the period liability before it is booked. The payroll specialist keeps the payroll run, the loonaangifte filing and the individual employee file.
data_needed: Payroll journal and loonaangifte totals by wage component and site
Wage-component map agreed with payroll
Latest Whk rate letter and pension rates from the CAOs
Headcount split between own staff and agency flex
Leave, vakantiegeld and sick-pay accrual rules
Prior-period signed tie-out
in_practice.logs_to: The payroll tie-out in the close folder on SharePoint: map version, rate letter, accounts, approver and time.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit Payroll calculates wage components, supports the loonaangifte and posts the payroll journal to the ledger.
Dutch employers reconcile the werknemersverzekeringen wage base and the related balance-sheet accruals to the payroll journal as part of the close and the audit.
DataSnipper matches source PDFs, such as tax assessments and rate letters, to amounts in an Excel tie-out.

risks: Payroll and sick-leave data are personal data. The tie-out should use component totals. Poortwachter files and health details stay out of Finance.
Flex workers pulled into the own-staff premium base, or own staff left out, move the Whk and wage-tax position.
A late Whk rate letter means an automated accrual on the old rate looks exact and is wrong.
US-style workers' compensation is the wrong frame. The Dutch items are Whk, loondoorbetaling during illness, and any private cover the company has actually bought.
research_questions: Which AFAS wage components are marked premium-bearing, and when was that map last checked against both CAOs?
By how many euros did last year's payroll accrual differ from the auditor's figure?
Is the Whk rate letter a PDF in a known SharePoint folder?
Can the tie-out run on totals by site and component so individual sick-leave records never reach Finance?

tasks.short: Advise management on the ledger effect of pay, benefits, systems and tax.

today.trigger: The Finance Director, HR Director or Compensation and Benefits Specialist asks what a proposal will do to the result. Typical subjects are a CAO wage step, a WKR benefit, a new cost-centre design, or a vennootschapsbelasting position. Estate planning is a private-client topic and does not arise for this BV role.
steps: Read the question and collect the AFAS balances, the CAO clause and the WKR space used.
Build one Excel scenario of the profit-and-loss, cash and balance-sheet effect.
Check with payroll or Compensation and Benefits when terms of employment are touched.
Talk it through with the controller and write a short note.
File the note on SharePoint next to the decision.
drudgery: Rebuilding the wage-cost model from an old file.
Searching SharePoint for the current CAO text and the WKR calculation.
Rewriting a verbal answer so the later journal matches what was advised.
today.time_sinks: Waiting for a reliable mix of own staff and flex by site, and advice that was given in Teams and never tied to the entry that was booked.

lenses.faster: The balances, the CAO clause, the WKR room and a first costing are in a one-page brief before the meeting. The meeting starts from the numbers.
lenses.autonomous: A Teams request can open a brief with the balances and the clause attached. The advice itself goes out only after the accountant has signed it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every CAO and benefit proposal would be costed before the works-council consultation, and a new cost type would be given a ledger treatment once, in a model the next question reuses.
lenses.joy: Hunting the prior workbook goes away. What people value is the session where a director decides with the numbers in the room.
lenses.options: The brief costs five routes: absorb it, pass it through in the rates, phase the CAO step, change the flex ratio, or use remaining WKR space, each with profit, cash and a works-council flag.
lenses.altitude: The accountant publishes the costing model and the accounting-policy choices, and tests new proposals against that model.
reach: The cost side of a compensation proposal that Compensation and Benefits now builds from scratch.
The accounting-treatment note the controller writes for the external auditor.

tasks.human_edge: The advice is trusted because the accountant will own the entry afterwards and sits with the director. Pay that touches a CAO or the works council is a consultation, and the accountant's job is the costing and the ledger treatment.
tasks.pattern_why: The work product is advice to management. A model can draft the costing and retrieve the clause. The accountant leads the conversation and signs the note. Plan design, the works-council process and any filing stay with HR, payroll and the external tax advisor.

in_practice.trigger: A written request from Finance, HR or Compensation and Benefits, with the proposal and the date a decision is needed.
steps: The brief pulls the relevant AFAS balances, headcount mix by site, WKR space used, and the CAO or policy clause from SharePoint.
Five costed routes are drafted, with profit, cash and balance-sheet effects, and a flag where WOR consent or advice applies.
The accountant corrects the assumptions with payroll or Compensation and Benefits.
The accountant walks through the brief with the controller or the director and edits the recommendation.
The signed note is filed next to the decision, labelled as management input and, where pay changes, as input to works-council consultation.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs every note before it is sent. No scenario is implemented from the draft. Tax filings stay with the external tax advisor. Pay-scheme decisions stay with HR and, where the WOR says so, the works council.
data_needed: Proposal text and who asked
AFAS balances and headcount by site and by own staff versus flex
WKR space used
Current CAO clauses and internal policies
Accounting policy for the topic
Whether the WOR requires consent or advice
in_practice.logs_to: The advice library on SharePoint, linked to the later journal entry where one is booked, with the signer and the date.

evidence.claim: Management accounting advice on the profit effect of a wage increase, the werkkostenregeling and a tax position is ordinary work for an internal accountant, with filings left to the payroll specialist or the external tax advisor.
Excel scenarios and Power BI what-if parameters can show several costed versions of one proposal from the same model.

risks: A fluent draft can be read as a tax opinion. The external tax advisor remains responsible for the filing position.
A costing that uses named employees is personal data. Scenarios should stay on grades, sites and groups.
Under the WOR, changes to a pay scheme need works-council consent. A fast model must be labelled as input to that consultation.
Health-plan design in the US sense does not exist here. The employer topics are the Zvw employer levy, WKR vitality arrangements, and the cost of loondoorbetaling.
research_questions: Of the advice requests in the last year, how many were CAO or WKR costings, how many were ledger or report design, and how many were tax?
Does Compensation and Benefits already keep a costing sheet this brief would duplicate?
Which of these decisions require works-council consent, and is that flag reliable enough to put on the brief?
Who may sign a vennootschapsbelasting position: this accountant, the Finance Director, or the external tax advisor?

tasks.short: Test a finance system change before go-live and say whether it will work.

today.trigger: A project asks Finance to sign before go-live. Typical changes are an AFAS approval flow, a cost-centre redesign, a Rabobank payment-batch change, or an interface that posts warehouse billing into AFAS.
steps: Read the process design on SharePoint.
List the controls that should work: approval, segregation of duties, VAT code, site and audit trail.
Sit with the key user in the AFAS test administration and try the main cases.
Write the gaps, including cases the design skipped.
Send the controller a go or a no-go.
drudgery: Writing test steps that repeat the policy.
Screenshotting AFAS screens.
Chasing the current version of the design.
today.time_sinks: Being asked in after the build is finished, and a test administration that does not contain a real multi-site invoice, a flex-worker accrual or a payment file with a cutoff.

lenses.faster: A test list, built from the control matrix and the design, is ready before the workshop. The workshop is spent trying to break the flow.
lenses.autonomous: A new design version filed in the project folder refreshes the test list and marks which controls have no test yet. A person still signs the go-live.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every finance change, including a small approval-limit edit, would be tested on real cases from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo before it reaches production.
lenses.joy: The screenshots and the rewritten test scripts go away. What remains is the attempt to break the design with a Sunday-night exception.
lenses.options: The review returns go, go-with-conditions, and no-go, each with the residual risk in euros and the condition that would clear it.
lenses.altitude: The accountant keeps the control matrix and the standard test set for AFAS finance changes, and reviews only the gaps a new design adds.
reach: The control section of a change request the controller now reviews alone.
The informal acceptance check the bookkeepers do on a new invoice workflow.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which exception will actually happen: a flex worker on a night shift, a missing goods receipt, or a payment file that still has to catch the Rabobank cutoff. That case is rarely in the design.
tasks.pattern_why: The accountant leads the review and signs go-live. Software can draft the test list and compare the design with the control matrix. Whether the evidence is enough depends on how the warehouses and the agencies work, which the specification does not capture.

in_practice.trigger: A project requests finance sign-off, or a new design version is saved in the project folder.
steps: The design is compared with the control matrix: approval, segregation of duties, VAT, site, audit trail, payment cutoff.
A test list is drafted, including the standard cases and the known exceptions (multi-site drop, agency hour mismatch, late goods receipt).
The accountant runs the list with the key user in the AFAS test administration and records what failed.
Gaps are written as go, go-with-conditions, or no-go, with the residual euro risk.
The controller receives the signed note. Conditions are retested before production.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the go-live note. The controller signs when the residual risk is above the threshold they have set. The build and the production move stay with the project.
data_needed: Current process design and the version under test
Finance control matrix
AFAS test administration with realistic documents
Approval limits, VAT codes and site structure
Rabobank batch cutoff rules
Open conditions from the last sign-off
in_practice.logs_to: The project folder on SharePoint: design version, test list, result of each case, residual risks accepted, signer and date.

evidence.claim: Dutch AFAS projects commonly test in a separate acceptation environment and review workflow and master-data changes before production.
A pre-implementation review against a control matrix is standard internal-audit practice for a finance system change.

risks: A test list that copies the design will miss the design's blind spots and give a false go.
A test environment copied from production can contain employee and bank data. Access and retention have to follow the AVG.
Sign-off without the bookkeepers who use the screen misses the failures that appear on the first real Monday.
research_questions: How many AFAS or payment-batch changes went live in the last year with a written finance sign-off, and how many were reversed?
Does the test administration hold realistic multi-site, agency and payment-file cases?
Above what residual euro risk does the controller still want to sign in person?
Did the last failed change fail on a case the design never mentioned?

tasks.short: Report how assets are used and what audits found, and recommend changes.

today.trigger: The monthly management meeting, an external-audit management letter, or a question about idle assets such as a trailer pool or a quiet hall in Tilburg.
steps: Pull the fixed-asset register from AFAS with cost, depreciation and cost centre.
Ask operations for utilization, or take the Excel file they last sent.
Update the list of open audit points and whether the agreed action was done.
Write two or three recommendations with a euro effect.
Send the note to the Finance Director and the controller.
drudgery: Refreshing the audit-point tracker by hand.
Reformatting the asset list by site.
Chasing three different definitions of utilization.
today.time_sinks: Utilization figures that cannot be tied to the asset register, and recommendations with no owner, so the same point returns next month.

lenses.faster: The asset register, the open audit points and a first recommendation are assembled when the close locks. The accountant edits the recommendation and the euro effect.
lenses.autonomous: The period lock refreshes the asset and audit pack. An audit action past its due date opens a line without someone rereading the tracker.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost management would see, each month and in one definition, what idle trailers, racking and hall space cost, and every audit point would have an owner and a euro amount.
lenses.joy: Chasing last month's action list goes away. What remains is the discussion with a site director about what to redeploy, sell or stop.
lenses.options: For each idle pool the pack shows hold, move to another site, or dispose, with the profit and cash effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets the utilization definition Finance will stand behind, and the rule for an overdue audit point, and reviews the exceptions.
reach: The management-letter status tracker the controller now keeps.
The first pass of a utilization note that operations now sends in its own format.

tasks.human_edge: A proposal to empty a hall, move trailers or change a shift is a decision for the site director, and it can require the works council. The accountant's edge is tying the choice to the ledger and stating which figure management can defend.
tasks.pattern_why: The register, the depreciation and the action tracker can be assembled on a schedule. A recommendation about operations goes to management only after the accountant has signed it.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period lock, or a new management letter saved to the audit folder.
steps: The job refreshes the fixed-asset register by site and cost centre, with cost, depreciation and net book value.
Utilization files that follow the agreed definition are joined on. Assets with no utilization file are listed as missing, not as zero.
Open audit points are aged. Actions past the due date are flagged with the owner.
Three options are drafted for material idle pools, with profit and cash effects.
The accountant edits the recommendations and sends the signed pack to the Finance Director and the controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs every recommendation before it goes to management. The figures on assets and on overdue actions refresh on the lock. Site directors decide what to do, and HR leads anything that changes rosters or headcount.
data_needed: Fixed-asset register with cost centre and site
Agreed utilization definition and the latest operations file
Depreciation and maintenance cost by asset group
Open audit points, owners and due dates
Materiality for what counts as idle
in_practice.logs_to: The management-pack folder on SharePoint, and the audit-point list with owner, due date, status, signer and time.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit's fixed-asset register holds acquisition cost, depreciation and cost centre, which is enough to report the ledger side of asset use by site.
Tracking management-letter points through to an owner and a due date is standard external-audit follow-up.
Power BI can present a register by site once the register is in the refreshed dataset.

risks: Warehouse fill and fleet use may live in operations files outside AFAS. A pack that treats missing use as zero will start the wrong argument.
A recommendation that changes shifts or staffing can require works-council consent. The pack has to say so before management treats it as decided.
A model that overstates an audit weakness damages the relationship with the external auditor.
Idle-asset advice that ignores maintenance and inspection dates, including vehicle inspections, is incomplete.
research_questions: Where do warehouse and fleet utilization figures live, and is there one definition for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo?
How many points from the last management letter are still open, and where are they tracked?
Which recommendations may go out on the accountant's signature, and which does the Finance Director want to see first?
When was the AFAS asset register last checked against what is physically at the three sites?

role.altitude: The accountant moves from rebuilding monthly packs to designing the checks, the maps and the thresholds the close runs on. The month is then spent on the judgments that change the forecast, the premium position or a go-live. FP&A and the Finance Director still own the forecast the business trusts.
reach: First-pass flux and budget-versus-actual commentary now written by FP&A.
The payroll accrual journal now posted by the bookkeepers from a payroll summary.
Duplicate-invoice and supplier-IBAN checks the bookkeepers do by eye.
The control section of an AFAS change the controller reviews alone.
The cost side of a compensation proposal Compensation and Benefits now builds from scratch.
The management-letter tracker the controller keeps by hand.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are about 220 hours a year per accountant, roughly one seventh of the role. The rest is the close itself: entries, VAT, fixed assets, intercompany and the statutory file. Automating this slice does not by itself cut days-to-close in half. Two people also cannot absorb payroll, the external tax opinion, credit decisions or the works-council process. The hard limit is data that is not in AFAS, especially agency portals and operational utilization, plus the sign-off the Belastingdienst and the auditor will still attribute to a named person.
skills_to_grow: Writing a wage-component map and a control matrix as rules someone else can run.
Enough AFAS, Power Query and the finance extract to challenge a published figure.
Dutch topics that sit beside payroll: Whk, loonheffingen, WKR, leave and vakantiegeld provisions, and inlenersbeloning.
Recognising when a workflow needs an AVG basis, works-council information, or a human decision under the EU AI Act.
role.ambitious_version: The two accountants run a continuous close for procure-to-pay, order-to-cash and payroll liabilities. Every material journal, agency invoice and premium accrual is tested in the week it happens. The management pack is a by-product of the lock. Their time goes to the few items that change the forecast or the tax position, which is what makes the forecast something the sites will trust, and what shortens the close.
